claims.text: Controlled post-deformation annealing refines the nanoscale precipitate distribution in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Refining the nanoscale precipitate distribution through post-deformation annealing improves ductility and uniform deformability.
The proposed annealing treatment can improve ductility without compromising high strength.
The proposed annealing treatment can preserve impact-induced energy release.
The as-deformed refractory high-entropy alloy has a relatively homogeneous microstructure.
Optimized post-deformation annealing induces a dual-phase microstructure.
Optimized post-deformation annealing produces finely dispersed nanoscale precipitates.
Finer, evenly dispersed precipitates facilitate additional slip systems.
Finer, evenly dispersed precipitates obstruct dislocation motion.
The precipitate-mediated obstruction of dislocation motion delays crack initiation.
The balance between enhanced slip and impeded dislocation motion increases ductility while retaining high strength.
Annealed samples will exhibit higher strain-to-failure than untreated samples.
Annealed samples will maintain yield strength comparable to untreated samples.
Annealed samples will maintain impact energy absorption comparable to untreated samples.
The untreated alloy has lower ductility and more localized deformation than the proposed annealed condition.
Excessive grain growth caused by annealing can degrade strength.
An uncontrolled phase transformation can degrade strength or alter energy-release characteristics.
The beneficial response depends on the alloy composition being within a range favorable for dual-phase formation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires preservation of impact-induced energy release, but the predicted outcome refers to impact energy absorption, and Charpy or drop-weight measurements primarily operationalize impact response or absorbed energy rather than energetic-material energy release. These quantities are conflated, so the proposed experiment does not unambiguously test the stated energy-release claim.
